It yields each non-empty line and a separate "\n" for every line break, so an empty line yields no value of its own and the empty document yields nothing (probe Text.of(["", ""]).iter() yields only "\n"; Text.empty.iter() yields nothing).

Returns a PartialTextCursor (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:106-108 (Text.iterRange), :475-517 (PartialTextCursor)) that runs a RawTextCursor backward when from > to, skips to the range start on the first next() and trims each value to the range; `to` defaults to length. from and to are not clipped: a range past the end yields nothing (probe iterRange(20, 30) on a 13-position document) and a range covering more than the document yields the whole document (probe iterRange(-5, 100)).

Wraps iter() when `from` is omitted, else iterRange(line(from).from, end) where end is the document end when to == lines + 1 (the default), 0 when to <= 1, and line(to - 1).to otherwise, never before the start, in a LineCursor (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:110-125 (Text.iterLines)); line numbers are 1-based and `to` is exclusive.
